title: Signature Trie data structure — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — A trie stores strings in a tree where each edge is one character and each root-to-node path spells a prefix. Shared prefixes share nodes, so 'archive', 'archives', and 'archival' overlap on the 'archiv' path. Tries answer prefix queries in time proportional to the prefix length plus the number of matches. title: Signature Prefix query evaluation — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — A prefix query walks the trie along the query characters; failure at any step means zero matches. From the arrival node, a depth-first collection gathers every word in the subtree. The walk costs O(p) for a prefix of length p, independent of vocabulary size. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Reversed trie for suffixes — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — Suffix search reuses the trie by inserting every word reversed, turning suffixes into prefixes of reversed strings. A suffix query then reverses its pattern and runs the ordinary prefix walk. One extra reversed index doubles the structure but keeps suffix lookups equally fast. title: Signature Autocomplete behavior — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — Autocomplete is prefix search plus ranking: the trie yields candidates and a scorer orders them by frequency or recency. Incremental typing reuses the previous subtree instead of restarting from the root. Debouncing input and caching subtrees keep keystroke-latency low on big vocabularies. title: Signature Wildcard prefix expansion — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — Patterns like 'pre*' compile to a prefix query: walk to the 'pre' node and collect the subtree. Bounded expansion caps the collected terms so a two-letter prefix cannot explode the query plan. Expansion turns user-friendly wildcards into efficient index operations. title: Signature Edge-labeled compression (radix tree) — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — A radix tree compresses trie chains of single-child nodes into multi-character edges. This cuts node count dramatically for large vocabularies while preserving the same prefix semantics. Compressed tries back many production autocomplete and routing-table implementations. title: Signature Suffix array alternative — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — A suffix array lists all suffixes of a text in sorted order, supporting substring queries by binary search. It uses less memory than a suffix trie at the cost of O(m log n) lookup for a pattern of length m. Suffix arrays power full-text indexes where a trie per document would be too heavy. title: Signature Aho-Corasick multi-pattern — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — Aho-Corasick extends the trie with failure links, finding all of many patterns in one linear scan of the text. Building the automaton is O(total pattern length); scanning is O(text length + matches). It is the standard tool for scanning streams against large keyword sets, from intrusion detection to content filters. title: Signature DAWG for whole vocabularies — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — A directed acyclic word graph merges equivalent trie subtrees, storing huge word lists in minimal space. Lookup stays trie-fast while memory drops by an order of magnitude on natural-language vocabularies. Spell checkers and morphology engines commonly ship their lexicons as DAWGs. title: Signature Case and accent folding — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — Prefix indexes usually fold case and strip diacritics so 'Archive' matches the prefix 'arch'. Folding happens once at index time and again per query, keeping both sides in the same normal form. Without folding, users must guess the exact capitalization of stored terms. title: Signature Ranked prefix results — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — Raw prefix matches can number in the thousands, so ranking by term frequency, document frequency, or click logs orders them. Top-k collection prunes the subtree walk once k good-enough candidates are found. Ranking turns prefix search from a dump into a useful suggestion list. title: Signature Fuzzy prefix tolerance — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — Fuzzy prefix search allows a few edits in the prefix, using a Levenshtein automaton walked alongside the trie. The automaton tracks the set of reachable edit states per trie node, pruning branches that exceed the budget. This forgives typos in the first characters typed, where plain prefix search fails hardest. title: Signature Suffix stripping for stemming — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — Stemmers strip known suffixes ('-ing', '-ed', '-s') to conflate inflected forms before indexing. Ordered rules with minimum-stem guards avoid turning 'sing' into 's'. Suffix handling at index time is what lets a query for 'run' match 'running'. title: Signature Prefix search in databases — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — B-tree indexes serve prefix queries naturally: 'LIKE 'arch%'' becomes a range scan from 'arch' to 'arch\uffff. The database seeks to the lower bound and scans forward until keys stop matching. No special structure is needed; the sorted order of the B-tree does the work. title: Signature Memory-mapped trie storage — Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Signature original — Large tries live on disk in memory-mapped files so the operating system pages in only the visited nodes. Node layouts use compact arrays of (char, child-offset) pairs to keep each node cache-friendly. This design serves billion-term prefix indexes from a single machine.
